messages:
Sam B: Heads-up — we've noticed ~20% of traces from the async-worker fleet drop all child spans after the outgoing HTTP call. Root span exists but downstream work looks missing. Anyone seen this pattern?
Priya K: Oof. Which worker image/version and language runtime? sounds like context propagation or sampler decision across threads.
Sam B: go-worker:v3.2.1, running on dedicated pool. Jobs kick off goroutines for background transforms.
Jorge R: Common gotcha: starting goroutines without passing ctx loses trace context. Are we using otelhttp or manual instrumentation?
Sam B: We use otelhttp for the HTTP client. The transform pipeline is manual and spawns goroutines in a loop.
Lena W: Quick checks: 1) Verify exporter is receiving spans (tempo/gateway). 2) Check sampler settings in the env of the process. 3) Search logs for "Dropped span" from the SDK.
observability-bot: autotag -> alert: trace-drop-rate spike on async-worker (service: async-worker, env: prod). Link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/alerts/trace-drop-rate
Priya K: Can you paste the OTEL env for the pod? e.g. OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_PROPAGATORS
Sam B: From one pod: `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio`, `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.05`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://tempo-otlp.internal:4317`, `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=b3,tracecontext`.
Jorge R: parentbased_traceidratio at 5% means child spans will be dropped if parent sampling decided no. If the root is present then sampling passed — odd. Could be exporter batching or buffer overflow when goroutines race to flush.
Lena W: Also check the SDK max queue/batch settings. For Go, look at `otlptracegrpc` client config or envs that modify batch size/timeout. If goroutines create spans then exit before the span is ended/force-flushed, they may never be exported.
Priya K: Another quick test: set `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` on a staging pod and reproduce a few runs. If child spans appear consistently, sampler was the issue. Also enable DEBUG logs for the otel SDK: `OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
Sam B: Will try `always_on` on a canary and repro. Any helpful grep searches in the logs to find dropped export events?
Lena W: Grep for "failed to export" or "span dropped" and also for "exporter timeout". Check Kubernetes events for OOMKill on those pods around job run time.
Jorge R: For code-level: ensure you propagate ctx into goroutine: `go func(ctx context.Context) { ctx = trace.SpanContextFromContext(ctx) ... }(ctx)` — actually better: `go func(ctx context.Context) { ctx = ctx; // use passed ctx
    // create child span with tracer.Start(ctx, "transform")
}(ctx)` — avoid `context.Background()` inside goroutines.
Priya K: Also check HTTP client middleware: if you do `req = req.WithContext(ctx)` before sending, otelhttp will propagate headers. Confirm downstream receives `traceparent` headers in request logs.
Sam B: I can pull a request sample — looks like traceparent header present when we hit the external service. But inside our transform goroutine we don't see any instrumentation.
Lena W: That points to local propagation loss. For immediate mitigation: 1) set `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` on a single canary to confirm. 2) add a short `tracer.ForceFlush` after job completion as workaround. 3) file a quick PR to pass ctx into goroutine creation sites.
Sam B: Thanks — I'll create the canary now and run a few jobs. If still broken I'll paste debug logs here. Also will open a PR for the ctx propagation change and tag you both.
Jorge R: Ping me on the PR, I can review quickly. If canary shows spans, we should schedule a patch for prod rollout with a telemetry test.
observability-bot: note -> playbook updated: "async-worker context-propagation checklist". Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/async-worker-propagation
Sam B: Added results: canary with always_on shows full child spans. With default sampling the drop rate returns. Going to proceed with PR to fix goroutine ctx and add a unit/integration test to assert spans exported.
Priya K: Perfect. When you have the PR link drop it here and add a short description of the repro steps so SRE can run the telemetry test during rollout.
Sam B: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
